items.title: Number of trees planted in Mississauga would form line stretching to Vancouver: city
items.summary: Mississauga officials say the number of trees planted across the city since the launch of the One Million Trees Mississauga initiative in 2013 would, placed end to end, form a line long enough to stretch all the way to Vancouver. In case you’re wondering, the tally of sugar maples, white pines, red oaks, paper birch and other native trees it takes to create such a formation, according to the City of Mississauga, is 653,729. That’s the up-to-date figure (as of this week) of trees planted the past 13 years since the initiative to add one million trees to the city’s canopy by 2032 was launched. The city reached the halfway mark nearly three-and-a-half years ago, in April 2023. Through the program, trees are planted by city staff, community partners and volunteers on both public and private property. The goal is to “help conserve and enhance the city’s open spaces and forested areas for future generations to enjoy,” the city said, adding residents can add to the total one planting at a time if they wish. “Whether you participate in a city tree planting event or plant on your private property, each tree counts. Add your tree to our tally and have it count towards the city’s goal of planting one million trees,” the city said. 2 million trees on both public and private lands across the city. And that number is growing as the municipality, conservation authorities, businesses, community groups, schools and individuals all contribute their tree-planting efforts.

items.title: New school board offices change how Mississauga and Brampton parents can escalate concerns
items.summary: Parents in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon now have a new way to get their concerns heard at the school board level, and the change is particularly significant in Peel, where both major school boards are currently under provincial supervision. Student and Family Support Offices officially launched across Ontario’s 72 publicly funded school boards on Sept. 1, giving parents and guardians a formal avenue to escalate concerns that have not been resolved at the school level. For families in Peel, however, the new system comes at a time when the traditional role of elected school trustees has been significantly altered. Both the Peel District School Board (PDSB) and Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board (DPCDSB) are under provincial supervision. At the PDSB, the province placed the board under supervision in January after concerns about its finances and governance. Heather Watt was subsequently appointed as supervisor. The DPCDSB has been under supervision since June 2025 following concerns about its deteriorating financial position. Rick Byers was appointed supervisor, and the board says decisions that would normally be made by trustees are being made by the supervisor, with the exception of denominational matters. That makes the new support offices particularly notable for Peel families. Traditionally, a parent with a problem at school would start with the teacher, then the principal and, if necessary, a superintendent. An elected trustee could also become a point of contact for families with unresolved concerns.

items.title: One of the largest Swiss Chalet restaurants to be demolished for development in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga residential development is slated to replace one of the largest Swiss Chalet restaurants in Canada. , a two-storey commercial plaza with a Swiss Chalet near Sherwood Village (previously Sheridan Centre). The development, which would include 142 back-to-back townhomes, a 10-storey apartment building with 241 units and a public park, was approved at the City of Mississauga’s Planning and Development Committee last week. , submitted to the city. Ward 2 Coun. Alvin Tedjo noted the Swiss Chalet is one of the largest in the country. “We are going to lose that, but that’s okay because I am sure there is lots of space across the street, over at Sherwood Village,” Tedjo said. Community members expressed concerns about the loss of the plaza and its businesses. Staff suggested that the nearby Sherwood Village mall is a main retail centre for the area. Sheridan Corporate Centre is a two-storey plaza at 2155 Leanne Blvd.

items.title: A City in Tune returns to celebrate the music and musicians that helped shape Mississauga
items.summary: The Museums of Mississauga exhibit runs from September 24 to December 27, 2026. Entertainment and activities | September 14, 2026 Back for the second year, A City in Tune: Mississauga’s Greatest Hits, returns to Adamson Estate from September 24 to December 27, 2026. Presented by the Museums of Mississauga, the exhibit explores the people, places and sounds that have helped define Mississauga’s music story. This all-new exhibition invites visitors to listen, reflect and learn about Mississauga’s impressive and diverse musical talent. Explore artifacts, instruments and archival materials from artists such as Triumph, Donna Grantis and Billy Talent. See large-scale portraits of some of the city’s best-known musicians, check out a map of iconic music venues and attractions, and listen to curated playlists featuring artists connected to Mississauga. Join the Museums team on Saturday, September 26 for the opening reception. This is your opportunity to be among the first to explore the exhibit and celebrate the homegrown talent, memorable moments and local stories behind Mississauga’s music history. A City in Tune: Mississauga’s Greatest Hits exhibition Adamson Estate 850 Enola Ave. m.
